scheme: sha256 over canonical JSON of the case spec
why: a holdout chosen or edited after seeing scores proves nothing

rounds.note: First sealed holdout. Spec released when round 1 is published.

what_this_proves: The case that scored a round is the case sealed before it, unedited. Recompute sha256 over the canonical JSON of the released spec and compare.
what_this_does_NOT_prove_in_round_1: Concealment. Round 1's holdout is drawn from CANDIDATES-TRIAGE.md, which is public, so a determined vendor could tune against the whole shortlist. Round 1 therefore gives timestamp integrity and no secrecy. From round 2 the holdout is drawn from discovery that is not published until release. Stated here rather than left for a reader to notice.
open_data_promise: Every sealed spec is released when the round it scores is published, so the corpus stays open and free on a one-round delay. A permanently secret corpus would make this benchmark unauditable, which is worse than the problem a holdout solves.
